full_judgment:
Mr. A.B.M. Khairul Haque J:- This is an application under Article 102(2)(a) of the Constitution Of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in respect of the order No.48 dated 14.5.2009, passed by the I Court, Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka, in Artha Zari Case No.230 of 2008, refusing to stay the further proceedings of the said execution case till disposal of Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997, filed by the defendant-judgment-debtor-petitioner's under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

2. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners, referring to his application, submits that the suit was decreed ex-parte against the judgment-debtor-petitioner as such, the petitioner filed a miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure but the respondent Bank without contesting the said miscellaneous case filed the execution case, whereupon the petitioner filed an application before the executing court, praying for staying the further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of the aforesaid miscellaneous case. But the learned Judge by his order no.48 dated 14.5.2009, without considering the facts and circumstances of the case, rejected his said application. He further submits that if the execution case proceeds then his miscellaneous case praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree, will be infructuous to the greatest prejudice to the petitioner. 

3. Heard the learned Advocate and perused the application and also the order no.48 dated 14.5.2009. 

4. It appears that the Miscellaneous Case praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 28.8.1996 was filed on 24.8.1997 and the execution case was filed on 21.7.1997. It appears that both the cases were filed long ago but the miscellaneous case filed under Order IX rule 13 will be infructuous if the execution case proceeds. In that view of the matter, we are of the opinion that the interest of justice will be met if we direct the concerned court to dispose of the miscellaneous case within a period of 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this order. 

5. Under the facts and circumstances, the learned Judge, 1st Court, Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka, is directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997 filed under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, within 6(six) months. Mean while the Execution Case No.230 of 2008, pending in the same Court, be stayed for a period 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this Order.

 6. With this observation and direction the writ petition is summarily disposed of. 

End.
